turn_text: Well, I'm really pleased to share with you and your listeners that were now the second largest caucus in Washington, D.C. And I think if I had told myself, let alone anyone else, that launching a caucus for Republicans to talk about climate would gain that much support. Nobody would have believed me. But I think it really shows you how anxious Republicans are to engage. Sometimes they struggle with how to engage. I think that's one of the beauties of the caucuses is it shows them how to engage in this in a really productive way with our other colleagues. And in a way where they don't need to feel like they've left their conservative values at the door. And I think that's really important for them. And so it's been a great success. We continue. We know we have lots of work to do. We know we'll have a fair amount of turnover in Congress this year. We want to make sure we're growing. As we do that, we want to make sure we're having meaningful caucus meetings and educating people and making it a caucus experience that they enjoy. Bob will tell you that there's a lot of caucuses in Washington and I'm part of the snowboard caucus and that's a lot of fun to talk about in Provo but I'm not sure we're changing the world and so we want to caucus quite frankly that changes the world and so it's fun to be part of that.
